name: Sublist3r - Passive Subdomain Enumeration
description: Sublist3r enumerates subdomains using OSINT sources (search engines, VirusTotal, DNSdumpster, Netcraft, ThreatCrowd, etc.) and optional brute force. Fast first-pass subdomain discovery that requires no direct contact with the target during the passive phase, feeding into live-host probing and content discovery.
notes:
=== BASIC (passive OSINT) ===
  sublist3r -d <domain>
  # Save results:
  sublist3r -d <domain> -o subdomains.txt

=== WITH BRUTE FORCE (subbrute) ===
  sublist3r -d <domain> -b

=== LIMIT TO SPECIFIC ENGINES ===
  sublist3r -d <domain> -e google,bing,virustotal

=== SCAN FOUND SUBDOMAINS FOR OPEN PORTS ===
  sublist3r -d <domain> -p 80,443

=== TYPICAL PIPELINE ===
  sublist3r -d <domain> -o subs.txt
  cat subs.txt | httpx -silent | nuclei

=== ALTERNATIVES / COMPLEMENTS ===
  subfinder  # faster, more sources, actively maintained
  amass enum # most thorough, active+passive
  assetfinder
  # Run several and merge/sort -u for best coverage

recommended.note: subfinder is faster with more sources.
Amass for the most thorough active+passive enum.
Probe which discovered subdomains are live.

defense.why_it_works: Passive enumeration queries third-party OSINT sources (CT logs, search engines, passive DNS), so the target sees little or no direct traffic. Brute-force mode does query the target resolver.
defense.impact: Maps the external DNS attack surface, revealing forgotten/dev/staging hosts.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1590.002] Passive phase is largely undetectable by the target. Brute-force mode causes many NXDOMAIN lookups against authoritative DNS from one resolver.
defense.artifacts: Authoritative DNS logs showing bursts of random subdomain queries (brute mode only); CT-log monitoring reveals attacker interest only indirectly.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=dns record_type=A
| stats count as queries dc(query) as unique by src_ip
| where unique > 500
defense.sentinel_kql:
DnsEvents
| where Name endswith "example.com"
| summarize Unique=dcount(Name) by ClientIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where Unique > 500
defense.prevention: Minimize public DNS records; monitor certificate transparency logs for your domains; decommission stale hosts; use wildcard DNS cautiously; split-horizon DNS for internal names.
